headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell overlap: Cursor can write/egress broadly while slim can read/write container artifacts, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files and clipboard contents, and slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and Dockerfiles. If slim outputs attacker-controlled text into shared files or logs, Cursor may treat it as trusted content. The pair has a filesystem bridge, so injection is plausible even without a documented direct parser exploit.
conditions: IF slim writes attacker-controlled instructions into a shared workspace file that Cursor opens
IF Cursor is run in a workflow that copies slim output into the clipboard or editor buffers
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic opening of slim-generated files in Cursor
Review slim output before copying into Cursor
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can send data to model providers and MCP servers; slim touches container images, filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and private keys. If they share a workspace, sensitive artifacts can flow from slim into Cursor’s outbound context. The pairwise leakage path is credible from profiles alone.
conditions: IF slim processes images containing secrets, keys, or environment variables in a directory Cursor can read
IF Cursor forwards those files or clipboard contents to external model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Run slim on sanitized images only
Disable Cursor access to secret-bearing paths
Use separate OS users for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists for Cursor

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have shell execution, filesystem write, and broad network egress. Cursor also modifies git state and runs inside the user editor process, while slim operates on container artifacts. In a shared directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other; the overlap is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout or workspace directory
IF Cursor Yolo mode and slim run concurrently against shared mutable files
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate checkout
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable Cursor Yolo mode during slim runs
Use ephemeral copies for slim analysis
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can act on generated content, and slim produces container-minification outputs and artifact changes. If Cursor treats slim’s output as authoritative, downstream edits or commands can propagate errors. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so cascading mistakes are plausible but not guaranteed.
conditions: IF Cursor consumes slim-generated reports or commands without human review
IF slim output is pasted into Cursor and then used to edit files or run shell commands
mitigations: Require human review before acting on slim output
Keep slim reports in a separate folder
Use a checklist for any Cursor action derived from slim
Turn off auto-run behaviors in Cursor
requires-engineering: add schema validation for slim outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, clipboard contents, and model-provider APIs, while slim handles container images, filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and private keys. If regulated data or secrets are present in those artifacts, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through external model calls. No profile shows a specific compliance control that prevents this.
conditions: IF regulated data, private keys, or customer secrets are present in files Cursor can read
IF Cursor sends those materials to external model providers or MCP servers without a DPA or retention control
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared workspaces
Confirm vendor DPAs and retention settings
Redact secrets before analysis
Use local-only models for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing
